name: Shezmu permissionless collateral mint
summary: A WBTC collateral input token exposed mint(address,uint256) without caller authorization. The attacker minted arbitrary collateral, deposited it into the vault, and borrowed unbacked ShezUSD.

loss.notes: The $4.9 million figure is the widely reported gross campaign loss across the affected ShezUSD and ShezETH pools. It is a face-value estimate for relatively illiquid protocol assets; the attacker later returned a substantial portion after negotiating a 20% bounty, which is not netted from the exploit-time loss.

lastCodeChange.description: The permissionless mint path is part of the token's immutable direct runtime, deployed in this transaction and unchanged through the exploit.

sources.note: Reviewed the live Ethereum transactions, receipts, call trace, target creation transaction, pre-exploit runtime and hash, deployed bytecode, independent exploit reproduction, project post-mortem, and reported loss. The previous anchor was a later transaction in the same campaign; 0x871ce0518bef66595ad5885a07d5699cbc71bffa7f8be732fc2565d087cb78ad is the earliest attack transaction identified by Shezmu and calls mint(address,uint256) on 0x641249db01d5c9a04d1a223765ffd15f95167924 before depositing the freely minted collateral. The direct runtime dispatches that public selector into its ERC-20 mint routine without caller authentication. The runtime was created at 20666529:69, contains no proxy delegation, and its pre-exploit hash matches the declaration. The project describes the same target and campaign; the $4.9 million reported amount is retained as gross face value, with negotiated recovery recorded separately.

limitations: The reported USD loss is a rounded face-value campaign estimate for illiquid protocol assets rather than an independently repriced onchain asset ledger.
